candidates.statement: Let C1 and C2 be tensor equivalent C ∗ -tensor categories endowed with an integral weak dimension function (e.g. they are finite semisimple tensor categories). Then C1 and C2 are also unitarily tensor equivalent. These theorems are interesting especially taking into consideration the fact that the abstract theorem 15.8 on which they rely uses only the choice of an integral weak dimension function on the affine Lie algebra fusion category. This category naturally admits such a dimension function given by representations of the simple Lie algebra g and no inner structure is needed in detail, other than the two cited milestone theorems.

candidates.statement: Let C be a semisimple pre-tensor category. An object ρ ∈ C is called generating if every simple object of C is a summand of some tensor power of ρ defined by some parenthesisation. A tensor power of ρ is an object defined as the result of iterative applications of the bifunctor ⊗ to pairs with entries ι or ρ. We define the order of a tensor power of ρ in a natural way. Different parenthesisations of the same order of two tensor powers of ρ are equivalent in a tensor category, thus it suffices to verify the generating property on a preferred choice of parenthesisation in this case, and is independent of the choice of the associativity morphism
